status: DRAFT, needs one-time owner approval; Spanish pending native review

q.en: Where does it stand right now?
q.es: ¿En qué punto está ahora?

questions.note: Built mechanically from the status line and the latest official action. The model never writes it.

q.en: What votes have there been so far, and what were the results?
q.es: ¿Qué votaciones ha habido hasta ahora y cuáles fueron los resultados?

questions.note: Every roll call on every vehicle under a written inclusion rule, never a selection. Counts and tallies come from the roll-call XML.

q.en: How did my senators and my representative vote?
q.es: ¿Cómo votaron mis senadores y mi representante?

questions.note: Rendered in the browser from the reader's ZIP (localStorage). No party labels. Never model-written.

q.en: What would a yes vote do, and what would a no vote do?
q.es: ¿Qué haría un voto a favor y qué haría un voto en contra?

questions.note: Answer from the pending vehicle's own text. A no vote is described by what the text would not do, never by predicted consequences.

q.en: What would change, and for whom?
q.es: ¿Qué cambiaría y para quién?

questions.note: Each provision tied to a section number. Sponsor fact sheets are navigation aids only, never wording.

q.en: What are the rules today, without this measure?
q.es: ¿Cuáles son las reglas hoy, sin esta medida?

questions.note: The status quo is where one-sided framing hides most easily; state it from law, court orders or CRS, not from either side's description.

q.en: What happens if Congress does not act?
q.es: ¿Qué pasa si el Congreso no actúa?

questions.note: Only what a law, rule or court order already says will happen. No forecasts.

q.en: What has to happen next for this to take effect?
q.es: ¿Qué tiene que pasar para que esto entre en vigor?

questions.note: Rules, not predictions. FUTURE_VOTE and speculation lints apply.

q.en: Would it go to the President, and what happens if it is vetoed?
q.es: ¿Llegaría al Presidente y qué pasa si lo veta?

questions.note: Distinguishes bills and joint resolutions (presented) from concurrent and simple resolutions (not presented).

q.en: What would it cost, and who made that estimate?
q.es: ¿Cuánto costaría y quién hizo ese cálculo?

questions.note: Fixed order: CBO, then the agency that bears the cost, each with its as-of date. Figures from a side are attributed. Absence of a CBO estimate is stated. When the measure itself spends nothing (war-powers resolutions, for example), the answer opens by saying so and labels every figure as the cost of the underlying activity, not of the measure.

q.en: What are supporters and opponents saying on the record?
q.es: ¿Qué han declarado de forma oficial y citable quienes lo apoyan y quienes se oponen?

questions.note: One question, both sides, by construction. Paired, primary sources first, roles not parties.

q.en: Are there other proposals on the same question?
q.es: ¿Hay otras propuestas sobre el mismo tema?

questions.note: Lists competing vehicles with their status. Listing is not endorsement; no call-to-action on non-corpus measures.

q.en: When would it take effect, and does any part of it expire?
q.es: ¿Cuándo entraría en vigor y vencería alguna parte?

questions.note: Both halves, always: when it takes effect (or that the text sets no delayed start date), then any sunset clauses, section by section.

q.en: How do the House and Senate versions differ?
q.es: ¿En qué se diferencian las versiones de la Cámara de Representantes y del Senado?

questions.note: Only when both chambers have text on the record.

q.en: Has Congress authorized the use of military force here?
q.es: ¿Ha autorizado el Congreso el uso de la fuerza militar en este caso?

questions.note: A statement about congressional action, not about the President's constitutional claims (see wp.admin_basis).

q.en: If it passes, does the President have to follow it?
q.es: Si se aprueba, ¿está obligado el Presidente a cumplirla?

questions.note: Contested legal question: CRS and the Constitution in our voice only as quoted; both sides' claims attributed.

q.en: What is the War Powers Resolution's 60-day limit, and how does it apply here?
q.es: ¿Qué es el límite de 60 días de la Resolución de Poderes de Guerra y cómo se aplica aquí?

questions.note: Explains the rule; whether the clock is running is attributed to each side.

q.en: What legal authority and goals has the Administration stated?
q.es: ¿Qué autoridad legal y qué objetivos ha declarado el Gobierno?

questions.note: Added so the bank carries the Administration's side as a question of its own, in its own words, attributed.

q.en: What would U.S. forces still be allowed to do?
q.es: ¿Qué seguirían teniendo permitido hacer las fuerzas de EE. UU.?

questions.note: Rules of construction and exceptions, per vehicle; vehicles differ.

q.en: What is the deadline, and what happens when it arrives?
q.es: ¿Cuál es la fecha límite y qué pasa cuando llega?

questions.note: The date comes from enacted text only.

q.en: If funding lapses, what keeps running and what pauses?
q.es: Si se acaba el financiamiento, ¿qué sigue funcionando y qué se suspende?

questions.note: From CRS shutdown reports and agency contingency plans, attributed by agency.

q.en: How long would the funding last?
q.es: ¿Cuánto tiempo duraría el financiamiento?

questions.note: End date as written in the text.

q.en: Would it override state laws?
q.es: ¿Prevalecería sobre las leyes estatales?

questions.note: Preemption and savings clauses both, quoted.

q.en: Who would enforce it, and how?
q.es: ¿Quién la haría cumplir y cómo?

questions.note: Agencies, private rights of action, penalties, as written.

q.en: Does it change how antitrust law applies?
q.es: ¿Cambia cómo se aplican las leyes antimonopolio?

questions.note: Say 'antitrust exemption' when the text says it; attribute the arguments.

q.en: Who qualifies, and what would they get?
q.es: ¿Quién cumpliría los requisitos y qué recibiría?

questions.note: Definitions section first.

q.en: How many people would it affect, according to official sources?
q.es: ¿A cuántas personas afectaría, según fuentes oficiales?

questions.note: Counts only from official sources, attributed when the source is a party to the dispute.

q.en: Would it change anyone's legal status?
q.es: ¿Cambiaría la situación legal de alguien?

questions.note: E.g. employee status, immigration status, tax status, as the text states.

q.en: What would change in everyday life?
q.es: ¿Qué cambiaría en la vida diaria?

questions.note: Concrete, text-backed effects only (e.g. rounding at the register), no predicted behavior.

q.en: How much does it authorize, and for what?
q.es: ¿Cuánto autoriza y para qué?

questions.note: Authorization is not appropriation; say which one the text is.
